questions: Are the movements you are making involuntary?
Do you feel an urge or inner discomfort before the movement occurs?
Can you briefly suppress the movement if you try?
Does suppressing it make the urge or discomfort worse?
Do you feel relief after making the movement?
Have these movements been happening repeatedly for more than a few days?
Did they begin suddenly?
Have the movements been getting worse recently?
Do they occur when you are resting as well as when you are active?
Do they become worse when you are anxious, stressed, or excited?
Do they decrease or stop while you are asleep?
Are similar movements occurring in your face, mouth, tongue, or legs?
Do you make involuntary sounds, clear your throat, or cough repeatedly?
Have you ever lost awareness or been unable to respond during an episode?
Have you had tongue biting, loss of bladder control, or confusion afterward?
Do you have weakness or numbness on one side of your body?
Do you have difficulty walking, speaking, swallowing, or coordinating your movements?
Have you recently had a head injury, fever, severe headache, or infection?
Have you started or increased any medication before these movements began?
Are you taking medication for nausea, vomiting, psychosis, depression, anxiety, or seizures?
Have you recently stopped taking any medication?
Have you used stimulants, recreational drugs, or unusually large amounts of caffeine?
Have you had similar movements in the past?
Does anyone in your family have similar movements or a neurological disorder?
Do these movements interfere with your daily activities?
Do they cause pain or injury?
Are you distressed or frightened by the movements?
Do you believe someone or something is controlling your movements?

results: 1. Complete bedside neurological examination, including strength, tone, reflexes, coordination, gait, eye movements, and characterization of the involuntary movements
coordination examination (limb and truncal): left upper-limb dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia; truncal coordination normal
cerebellar signs (dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia): dysmetria and dysdiadochokinesia in the left upper limb
kinetic / intention tremor (finger-nose): present and worse on reaching
tremor frequency estimate: slow, under about 4.5 Hz, with a wing-beating quality
effect of alcohol on the tremor: no effect
2. Urgent noncontrast CT scan of the head
CT head: decreased-size left thalamic tuberculoma
3. MRI of the brain with diffusion-weighted, susceptibility-weighted, and contrast-enhanced sequences
MRI brain with gadolinium: decreased-size left thalamic tuberculoma with no gliosis
brain MRI: thalamic lesion (tuberculoma) that DECREASED in size after anti-tuberculous treatment, with no gliosis
4. MRI or CT angiography of the head and neck
5. Complete blood count, electrolytes, glucose, calcium, magnesium, renal function, and liver function tests
serum electrolytes, urea and creatinine: normal
serum calcium, magnesium and phosphate: normal
6. C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate
10. Serum antistreptolysin O and anti-DNase B titers
11. Serum autoimmune encephalitis and neuronal antibody panel
serum paraneoplastic / neuronal autoantibody panel: normal
12. Lumbar puncture for cerebrospinal-fluid cell count, protein, glucose, culture, viral PCR, oligoclonal bands, and autoimmune encephalitis antibodies
CSF cell count and differential: normal
CSF oligoclonal bands and IgG index: normal
CSF culture and viral PCR: normal
14. Review of all recently discontinued medications and their withdrawal effects
medication, supplement and herbal history: nothing relevant
15. Trial of restarting the discontinued medication under monitored neurological supervision
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Holmes (rubral) tremor caused by a left thalamic tuberculoma, despite radiological regression after antituberculous treatment

ALTERNATIVE 1: Cerebellar outflow tremor secondary to thalamic tuberculoma

ALTERNATIVE 2: Parkinsonian tremor due to thalamic–nigrostriatal pathway involvement

ALTERNATIVE 3: Functional tremor with coincidental thalamic tuberculoma
